propositions: reconcile-bridge-canary.yml contains ~200 lines of production logic in YAML run-blocks (staleness classification, two alert-ticket lifecycle state machines) that are untestable and unlintable.
The canary workflow logic interleaves ${{ }} expressions with branchy decision logic (API-error vs zero-state vs stale; dedup-find vs open vs comment vs close), creating maintenance and defect risk.

Strangler-fig migration extracts classification and alert-lifecycle logic into scripts/canary_bridge.py subcommands (check-heartbeat, heartbeat-alert, check-binding-drift, binding-drift-alert) while preserving CAS push loops in YAML and adding unit test coverage.

Error handling dispositions are preserved per YAML step: alert-write failures fail loud; dedup finds degrade to empty on CLI failure; bridge-fsck exit 1 with valid JSON is treated as drift signal (not error); DRY_RUN gates apply at both step and subcommand level.

Anti-rot test pins the canary wiring (workflow parses, steps invoke canonical Python entry point, flush loop byte-identical); parity verified post-merge via workflow_dispatch run showing identical staleness classification and alert behavior.
